comment: The description of the European cross-border infrastructure is accurate. Since the entry into force of Regulation (EU) 2025/327, cited at footnote 33, the separation of primary and secondary use that lines 922–924 describe is a legislated obligation for participating states rather than an accompanying legal framework, with consequences for how national components are specified. Countries planning for cross-border exchange may find it useful for the guidance to note that a regional legal framework can impose specification requirements on national DPI-H components, and that this is now the case in one region.

public.text: The description of the European cross-border infrastructure is accurate. Since the entry into force of Regulation (EU) 2025/327, cited at footnote 33, the separation of primary and secondary use that lines 922–924 describe is a legislated obligation for participating states rather than an accompanying legal framework, with consequences for how national components are specified. Countries planning for cross-border exchange may find it useful for the guidance to note that a regional legal framework can impose specification requirements on national DPI-H components, and that this is now the case in one region.
public.suggestedRevision: Amend lines 922–924 to note that in the European Union this framework is now established in regulation, and add a sentence: "Where a regional legal framework of this kind applies, its requirements should be treated as inputs to national component specifications from the outset rather than as a later compliance exercise."
